question.problem:
Consider the function $y = \dfrac{(x+3)^3}{(x+5)^6}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
y' = -\dfrac{g(x)(x+3)^2}{(x+5)^7}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y =  \dfrac{(x+3)^3}{(x+5)^6}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{(x+3)^{3}}{(x+5)^{6}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+3)^{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+5)^{6}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+3)-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+3)-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+5)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =3\cdot \frac{1}{x+3}-6\cdot \frac{1}{x+5} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{3}{x+3}-\frac{6}{x+5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for $y'{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{3}{x+3}-\frac{6}{x+5})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y =  \dfrac{(x+3)^3}{(x+5)^6}{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{(x+3)^{3}}{(x+5)^{6}}(\frac{3}{x+3}-\frac{6}{x+5}) \\  & =\frac{(x+3)^{3}}{(x+5)^{6}}(\frac{3(x+5)-6(x+3)}{(x+3)(x+5)}) \\  & =\frac{(x+3)^{3}}{(x+5)^{6}}(\frac{-3x-3}{(x+3)(x+5)}) \\  & =-\frac{3(x+1)(x+3)^{2}}{(x+5)^{7}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x) = \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{3(x+1)}.
$$
